reviews.body: The interrupt fix introduces a custom failure-decoding regression that can break workflow replay.

review_comments.body:
[P1] Preserve custom failure decoding for non-default payload converters

When a caller supplies both a non-default payload converter and a custom failure converter, this branch now falls through to code that discards the caller's `from_failure`. For example, combining the existing `DomainFailureConverter` with `pydantic_data_converter` previously decoded recorded failures as `DomainError`, but now produces `ApplicationError`, for both client and replayer. This changes exception-handling branches during replay and can break existing workflows. Add Strands-specific failure handling without replacing custom decoding on this previously preserved path.

comments.body:
[![CLA assistant check](https://cla-assistant.io/pull/badge/signed)](https://cla-assistant.io/temporalio/ai-integrations?pullRequest=392)
All committers have signed the CLA.

Good catch, thanks. Fixed in 50d2ad0 and d6a8a63: on the non-default payload converter path the caller's failure converter is no longer replaced. A `DefaultFailureConverter` subclass gets the Strands handling mixed in on top (`StrandsFailureConverter` first in the MRO), so `to_failure` for other exceptions and `from_failure` are still the caller's, and your `DomainFailureConverter` + `pydantic_data_converter` example decodes `DomainError` again for both client and replayer. A converter that does not build on `DefaultFailureConverter` is kept exactly as supplied. Running the plugin twice keeps the wrapped class. New tests cover both cases; `tests/test_plugin.py`: 18 passed, ruff clean.

This reply was drafted with the help of an AI assistant (Claude Code).
